errors.claim_in_draft: Indonesia's national specialist doctor deficit is 65,000 as of 2023

primary_sources.key_data: Kemenkes stated deficit of 31,481 specialist doctors as of June 2023; 46,200 active specialists (STR-registered as of April 2023)
primary_sources.verbatim_quote: Untuk melayani 277 juta penduduk Indonesia, kita masih kekurangan dokter spesialis. Di mana ketersediaan saat ini 46.200 dokter spesialis, kita masih kekurangan sekitar 31.481 dokter spesialis secara total
primary_sources.official_source_person: Oos Fatimah, Direktur Penyediaan Tenaga Kesehatan, Kemenkes

primary_sources.key_data: Health Minister Budi Gunadi Sadikin stated deficit of 29,000 specialist doctors as of May 2024; annual production only 2,700/year
primary_sources.verbatim_quote: Masalah banyaknya dokter spesialis yang kurang. Salah satu penyebab kurang memang produksi dokter spesialis kita 2.700 per tahun, kebutuhan kita 29.000, 30.000.

errors.corrected_figure: ~31,481 specialist doctor deficit as of June 2023 (Kemenkes press conference); ~29,000 as of May 2024 (Health Minister statement). Active specialists: 46,200 (April 2023 STR). IDI figure ~30,546 is consistent.
errors.note_on_65000: The figure '65,000' likely conflates two different metrics: (a) the TOTAL number of specialist doctors needed (~78,000 at WHO ratio for 280M population) vs. (b) the DEFICIT above current supply (~31,481 in 2023). The 65,000 figure does not appear in any Kemenkes or IDI primary source.
errors.suggested_revision: Replace '65,000 medical specialist shortfalls nationally as of 2023' with: 'Indonesia's Ministry of Health reported a deficit of ~31,481 specialist doctors as of June 2023 (Kemenkes press conference, 26 June 2023), with only 46,200 specialist doctors active against a requirement of ~77,681 for a population of 277 million; the Health Minister reconfirmed a ~29,000 shortfall in May 2024.'

metric_clarification.what_this_measures: NCD-positive at screening: percentage of screened Peka B40 participants found to have at least one NCD (diabetes, hypertension, high cholesterol, or obesity) during the screening visit
metric_clarification.what_it_does_not_measure: This is NOT the NCD 'newly identified' rate (many may have known diagnoses) and NOT the 'enrolled to follow-up' rate. It is the NCD prevalence/positive rate among B40 adults aged 40+ who presented for screening.
metric_clarification.note_on_41pct: The 41% figure is not corroborated by any primary source retrieved. It may stem from an earlier programme phase (pre-2023), a subset metric (e.g., newly diagnosed only), or a misread of a different dashboard indicator. The KKMNOW dashboard (data.moh.gov.my/dashboard/peka-b40) returned HTTP 402 and could not be directly accessed to check for a 41% sub-metric; tagged [NEEDS-ATTENDED-FETCH] for direct dashboard verification.
